The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 44 / 2011-12 dated 03.07.2023 in respect of Survey No.106/1 measuring 1091 Square feet of Amruthahalli village, Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No. 106/1 measuring 1091 Square feet situated at Amruthahalli village, Yelahanka Hobli A.P. No.38/2024 has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010.

Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a compensation for the acquired land at the rate of Rs.300 lakhs per acre for agricultural land and Rs. 1,927/- per acre for converted land as compensation for the acquired land belongs to the petitioner.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application on 03.01.2012 for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs. 15,000/- per Square feet.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.

.3. Thereafter, the Arbitrator held an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-42 / 12(A), 12, 44, 43 / 2011-12 dated 03.07.2023.
.4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
A.P. No.38/2024 :GROUNDS:

The petitioner claims that the learned Arbitrator committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents by the petitioner side for deciding the market value and enhancing the market value in the proceedings before him while passing the market value in the proceedings before him while passing the impugned award.

Further the Arbitrator overlooking the statutory provision of law as contained in Section 3G (7)
(a) has illegally granted enhancement and fixed the compensation of Rs.3,323/- per Square feet against the award of respondent No.2 along with 9% interest from the date of taking possession.

Further the Arbitrator failed to consider the fact that in spite of land was converted for non-agricultural land, the respondent No.2 has awarded compensation under non developed area at the rate of Rs.1,927/- instead of Rs.3,323/- per Square feet.

Further the finding given by the learned Arbitrator is against the observation made by the A.P. No.38/2024 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka that, in determining the market value the use / category of the land as on Prema vs The Project Director Technical ... on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110807415/

Further the Arbitral Award dated 03.07.2023 is contrary to the substantive provisions of law and is patently illegal which is required to be set aside.
Among other grounds, prayed for reconsidering the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.

.5. The respondent No.1 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No.2 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.

Further the respondent No.1 initially being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award had preferred A.P. No.36/2023 before this Court on 20.09.2023 itself and this Court issued notice to the petitioner on the A.P. No.38/2024 same date and subsequently the summons were duly served upon the petitioner who remained absent on 03.01.2024 and 26.03.2024 and accordingly the petitioner was placed exparte ad the matter was posted for arguments.
Further the petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.6. The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No.1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

.7. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, she stated that the above A.P. No.38/2024 Arbitration Petition is filed within the limitation period of 90 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order and the Arbitrator has not sent the order copy of the award to the petitioner.

Now the petitioner filed the application before the Arbitrator for certified copy of arbitration award and received the same on 01.07.2024 and hence the appeal is within limitation from the date of application filed for certified copy of award and accordingly prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.

.8. The respondents have not filed any objections to the above Interlocutory Application No.1.
.9.

The respondent No. 1 to 3 though served with the notice, the respondents 1 and 2 appeared through their counsel, the respondent No.3 not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, the respondent No.3 has been placed exparte.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-44/2011-12 dated 03.07.2023.

1) Whether the petition filed by the petitioner is within time ?

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Points No.1 : In the affirmative Points No.2 : In the negative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .12. POINT NO.1: Perused the I.A. No.1 along with affidavit that has been filed for condonation of delay in filing the petition, satisfied with reasons therein and the said application is not opposed by the respondent No. 1.
Accordingly, I am of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to condone the delay in filing the petition.
Accordingly the point No. 1 is answered in the affirmative.
.13. POINT No.2:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The petitioner Smt. Prema is an owner of the property bearing Sy.
No.106/1 measuring A.P. No.38/2024 to an extent of 1091 Square feet of Amrthahalli village,
Yelahanka Hobli, Bengaluru North Additional Taluka and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-7 under Preliminary Notification dated 09.12.2009 and Final Notification dated 02.07.2010, is an admitted fact.

It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 1,927/- per Square feet for the acquired land.

sentences.text: It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.21,02,357/- in respect of 1091 Square feets was disbursed to the petitioner as compensation.

.14. Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioner Smt. Prema filed an application on 03.01.2012 before the respondent No.3 claiming that she is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 15,000/- per Square feet.

On the basis of said application, the respondent No.3 hold an enquiry and passed order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/44/ 2011-12 A.P.
No.38/2024 dated 03.07.2023.
The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.3,323/- per Square feet from Rs. 1,927/- per Square feet and awarded additional compensation of Rs. 1,396/- per Square feet.

4 .15.

The petitioner in the petition generally claimed that the Arbitrator not properly considered the documents produced by the petitioner for enhancement of compensation but entire petition nowhere discloses that what are the documents that have been produced by the petitioner before the LAO that has not been considered by the LAO while passing the award.
Apart from that what is the actual market value that ought to have been awarded by the LAO is also not properly and satisfactorily explained.

This court received the entire records from the office of the Arbitrator and the said file also nowhere discloses any documents have been submitted by the petitioner before the LAO to consider the market value.

In the absence of any such documents placed before the Arbitrator by the petitioner, certainly the petitioner can not claim that the A.P. No.38/2024 Arbitrator have not considered the documents because no documents were there before the Arbitrator to consider to determine the market value of the acquired property.

In fact, the claim of the petitioner before the Arbitrator is that market value of the acquired property is about Rs.4000/-
to 6000/- per Square feet but no documents have been placed either before the Arbitrator or before the LAO or along with this petition to substantiate the said fact.
In the absence of any such materials, certainly, the said claim of the petitioner cannot be accepted.

Apart from that the LAO fixed the rate at Rs.3,000/- per Square feet and added 50% as well as 25% to the said market value holding that the said property is abutting to National Highways, as such, certainly the Arbitrator has properly considered the market value of the acquired property.
.16. At this juncture, it is relevant to note that the respondent No.1 also challenged the award passed by the Arbitrator/respondent No.3 in L.A.C. No. 36/2023.

Subsequently the respondent No.1 not A.P. No.38/2024 pressed the said petition in view of payment of the compensation amount as per the arbitration award and got dismissed the petition as per order dated 21.11.2024.

In view of the said fact, it is clear that the petitioner received the compensation awarded by the Arbitrator and utterly failed to make out any case to show that the property is valued more than the market value determined by the Arbitrator.
In fact absolutely there is no material whatsoever on record to intervene with the award passed by the respondent No.3 and the said award is liable to be confirmed.
Accordingly, the above point No.2 is held in the negative.
.17. Point No.3:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Interlocutory Application No.1 filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is hereby allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is hereby dismissed.
Consequently, the impugned award passed by the Arbitrator/respondent No.3 in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/44/2011- 12 dated 03.07.2023 is hereby confirmed.
Parties to bear their own cost.
Office is directed to send back the Lower Court Records.
